mainTopic: The source for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's argument about לחם הפנים, the משנה on the חביתין, שבת and the כלי שרת, and the measurements and arrangement of the לחם הפנים on the שולחן
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about דוד eating the לחם הפנים at נוב. He was allowed only because his life was in danger. The גמרא then concludes that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree based on different received traditions. It proves this from רבי שמעון's wording, 'one should always be accustomed to say.' A new משנה follows. It teaches that the kneading, shaping and baking of the חביתי כהן גדול override שבת, but grinding and sifting do not, and רבי עקיבא gives the general rule behind this. The same משנה adds that the steps of the מנחות done inside the עזרה use a כלי שרת. It then gives the sizes of the שתי הלחם, the לחם הפנים and the שולחן, with רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר arguing over how the loaves were folded onto the table. It also describes the golden panels and rods that held the bread. The גמרא finds the source for using a כלי in a פסוק in יחזקאל. Finally, רבי יוחנן calculates how high the שולחן's holiness reaches, and the גמרא answers challenges from the rods, the air gaps, the בזיכין and the קרנות.

steps.title: דוד was allowed to eat because he was in danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining how דוד could eat the holy לחם הפנים: he was in mortal danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: [I was allowed to eat it because] I am in danger.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of an earlier explanation. It tells us why דוד was allowed to eat the holy bread at נוב: he was in danger from hunger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-כהן is normally forbidden to eat קדשים. When a life is in danger (פיקוח נפש), that rule is set aside. So דוד's eating does not show that the bread was not holy. It was permitted only because of the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Saving a life, which overrides almost every prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'he' here refers to דוד speaking about himself, so in practice it means 'I am in danger.'

phrases.english: He is in danger.
phrases.notes: This is דוד speaking about himself, so read it as 'I am in danger.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous part of the daf about דוד at נוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד ate the holy bread only because his life was in danger.

steps.title: The two sages disagree based on tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון are not arguing about how to read פסוקים. Each one received a different tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree based on a received tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us where the disagreement between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון comes from. It comes from different traditions they received from their teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא had tried to connect their argument to פסוקים, such as the story of דוד. Now it drops that approach. The question is whether the oven makes the לחם הפנים holy, and on that question each sage simply had a different tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on a received tradition passed down from teachers

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that not every argument between תנאים comes from reading פסוקים. Some come from different oral traditions.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
disagree based on a tradition.
phrases.notes: Here 'גמרא' doesn't mean the Talmud. It means a teaching they received from their teachers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּגְמָרָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside the proof from דוד, the גמרא concludes that the argument is based on tradition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument over whether the oven makes the לחם הפנים holy comes from different received traditions, not from פסוקים.

steps.title: Proof from the wording 'always be accustomed to say'
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's wording sounds like a repeated tradition, which supports the idea that the argument is based on tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording supports this. It teaches: רבי שמעון says, one should always be used to saying that the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are fit if made in the עזרה and also fit if made in בית פאגי. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the exact words of רבי שמעון's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'always be accustomed to say' sounds like a set teaching that is memorized and repeated. A teaching like that comes from tradition, not from reading a פסוק. That fits the conclusion in the previous step.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording also shows this (a precise reading of the text)
The two loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
An area outside the Temple courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about the oven and the לחם הפנים is based on tradition. The proof is רבי שמעון's wording, 'always be accustomed to say.'

phrases.english: It is also precise, for it teaches:
Rabbi Shimon says:
One should always be accustomed to say
the two loaves and the showbread
are fit if made in the Temple courtyard
and are fit if made in Beit Pagei,
phrases.notes: בית פאגי is a place outside the Temple courtyard, so even baking there is fine.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 2 from the wording of רבי שמעון's teaching.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון's opinion is based on tradition
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'לעולם הוי רגיל לומר' in רבי שמעון's statement

steps.title: Which steps of the כהן גדול's griddle-cakes override שבת
steps.stepSummary: Kneading, shaping and baking the חביתי כהן גדול are done in the עזרה and override שבת. Grinding and sifting do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The כהן גדול's griddle-cakes: their kneading, shaping and baking are done inside, and they override שבת. Their grinding and sifting do not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches which steps of making the כהן גדול's daily offering may be done on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kneading, shaping and baking may be done on שבת. Once the dough is made holy in a כלי, it would become פסול if left overnight, so these steps cannot be done ahead of time. Grinding and sifting the flour can easily be done before שבת, so they do not override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering
Override שבת (may be done even on שבת)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The High Priest's griddle-cakes:
their kneading, their shaping and their baking are done inside,
and they override Shabbat.
Their grinding and their sifting
do not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל לִישָׁתָן וַעֲרִיכָתָן וַאֲפִיָּיתָן בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading, shaping and baking the חביתין override שבת. Grinding and sifting do not.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's general rule about overriding שבת
steps.stepSummary: Anything that could have been done before שבת does not override שבת. Anything that could not be done before שבת does override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא stated a rule: any work that can be done on ערב שבת does not override שבת. Work that cannot be done on ערב שבת does override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא turns the details of the previous step into one general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the work could have been done before שבת. Grinding can be done early, so it does not override שבת. Baking cannot be done early because the bread would become פסול overnight, so it does override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden type of work on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's rule: if it could have been done before שבת, it does not override שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is a key principle across ש״ס for deciding when a מצוה overrides שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva stated a principle:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת –
phrases.english: Any work that can be done on Shabbat eve
does not override Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת –
phrases.english: and work that cannot be done on Shabbat eve
overrides Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific cases of step 4 into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work that could have been done before שבת does not override שבת. Work that could not have been done before does.

steps.title: Inside steps use a כלי שרת, outside steps do not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: the steps of the מנחות done inside the עזרה involve a כלי שרת, and those done outside do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the מנחות have use of a כלי inside, and do not have use of a כלי outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The same משנה continues with another rule. The preparation steps done inside the עזרה use a holy כלי, while the steps done outside do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי שרת makes what is placed in it holy. Steps done inside the עזרה, like kneading the חביתין, are done in a כלי שרת. Steps done outside, like kneading the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים, are not done in a כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Use of a holy Temple vessel (כלי שרת)

phrases.english: All the meal offerings:
they involve use of a vessel inside,
and they do not involve use of a vessel outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מַעֲשֵׂה כְלִי בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same משנה moves on to a new rule about using a כלי for the מנחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Preparation steps of the מנחות done inside the עזרה use a כלי שרת. Steps done outside do not.

steps.title: The measurements of the two breads
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the length, width and corner 'horns' of the שתי הלחם and of the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שתי הלחם is 7 טפחים long and 4 טפחים wide, with horns 4 fingers high. The לחם הפנים is 10 טפחים long and 5 טפחים wide, with horns 7 fingers high.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the exact sizes of the two special breads of the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each bread gets three numbers: length, width, and the height of its corner 'horns'. Length and width are measured in טפחים (handbreadths), and the horns are measured in smaller units called אצבעות (fingerbreadths).

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves brought on שבועות
The shewbread placed on the שולחן every שבת
'Horns', dough protrusions at the corners of the loaf
Fingerbreadths, a smaller unit than a טפח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the units. The length and width are in טפחים, but the horns are in אצבעות, which are much smaller.

phrases.english: The two loaves: their length is seven handbreadths,
and their width is four handbreadths,
and their horns are four fingerbreadths.
phrases.notes: The 'horns' are bits of dough sticking up from the corners of the loaf.

phrases.english: The shewbread: its length is ten handbreadths,
and its width is five handbreadths,
and its horns are seven fingerbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה moves on to the measurements of the breads.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שתי הלחם: 7 × 4 טפחים with 4-אצבע horns. לחם הפנים: 10 × 5 טפחים with 7-אצבע horns.

steps.title: A memory trick for the numbers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives letter codes so the measurements are not forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: so you won't make a mistake, remember זד״ד for the שתי הלחם and יה״ז for the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a short code made of letters to help remember the six numbers from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for its number value: ז=7, ד=4, י=10, ה=5. זד״ד means 7 long, 4 wide, 4 horns, and יה״ז means 10 long, 5 wide, 7 horns. It adds no new הלכה. It is only a memory aid.

keyTerms.meaning: So that you will not make a mistake

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: so that you will not err:
Zayin, dalet, dalet;
phrases.notes: The letters' number values are 7, 4, 4, which give the length, width and horns of the שתי הלחם.

phrases.english: yod, heh, zayin.
phrases.notes: These are 10, 5, 7, the numbers for the לחם הפנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory aid for the measurements just listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זד״ד = 7, 4, 4 for the שתי הלחם; יה״ז = 10, 5, 7 for the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: The shewbread must have flat sides
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא learns from the words 'לחם פנים' that the bread must have faces, meaning sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן זומא says: the פסוק says 'Put לחם פנים on the table before Me always.' It is called 'לחם פנים' because it must have 'faces'.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא brings a פסוק to teach something about the shape of the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the name 'לחם פנים' as 'bread with faces'. This means the loaf must have real sides, so it can't just be a rounded lump. So the name of the bread tells us its shape.

keyTerms.meaning: Faces, meaning the sides of the loaf
The golden table in the מקדש

phrases.english: Ben Zoma says:
"And you shall place on the Table
phrases.notes: שמות 25:30

phrases.english: shewbread before Me always":
"Lechem panim" means that it should have faces.
phrases.notes: 'Faces' here means flat sides, so the loaf isn't round.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר: וְנָתַתָּ עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן לֶחֶם פָּנִים לְפָנַי תָּמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about the shape of the לחם הפנים, learned from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לחם הפנים must have sides ('faces'), as its name shows.

steps.title: The table and the bread are the same size
steps.stepSummary: The שולחן is 10 by 5 and the לחם הפנים is also 10 by 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שולחן is 10 long and 5 wide. The לחם הפנים is 10 long and 5 wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the size of the שולחן next to the size of the bread. This sets up the next step, which explains how the bread was placed on the table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers are in טפחים. Since table and loaf have the same size, you might think the loaf just sits flat on it. But there are two rows of loaves, so the next step has to explain how they fit.

phrases.english: The Table: its length is ten and its width is five;
phrases.notes: The numbers are in טפחים, handbreadths.

phrases.aramaic: לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים – אׇרְכּוֹ עֲשָׂרָה, וְרׇחְבּוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: the shewbread: its length is ten and its width is five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the bread itself to the table it is placed on, setting up how they are arranged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שולחן is 10 × 5 טפחים, and so is each loaf of לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Laying the long bread across the table
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, the loaf's length is laid across the table's width, and the extra is folded up on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lays the loaf's length across the table's width. He folds up two and a half טפחים on one side and two and a half on the other. So the loaf's length fills the table's width. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the 10-טפח loaf is placed on the 5-טפח-wide table, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaf is 10 long, but the table is only 5 wide. So 5 טפחים stick out, and they are split up: 2½ are folded upward on each side. The loaf covers the table's width and its folded ends stand up like walls.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch: the loaf's LENGTH goes along the table's WIDTH, not along its length. That is exactly why there is extra dough to fold up.
steps.whatToRemember: Each loaf of לחם הפנים is 10 × 5 טפחים. According to רבי יהודה, it is laid across the 5-wide table with 2½ טפחים folded up on each side.

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אׇרְכּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד רׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוּלְחָן,
phrases.english: He places its length across the width of the Table,
and folds up two and a half handbreadths on this side
and two and a half handbreadths on that side,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצָא אׇרְכּוֹ מְמַלֵּא רׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוּלְחָן,
phrases.english: so it turns out that its length fills the width of the Table,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹתֵן אׇרְכּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד רׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוּלְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the measurements from step 10 to explain how the bread was arranged on the table.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the loaf's 10-טפח length lies across the table's 5-טפח width, with 2½ טפחים folded up on each side.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's measurements of the table and the bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the שולחן is 12 by 6 טפחים, and the לחם הפנים is 10 by 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: The table is twelve handbreadths long and six wide. The showbread is ten long and five wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion, רבי מאיר, about the size of the שולחן and the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees with רבי יהודה about the bread, 10 by 5. He disagrees about the table, making it bigger, 12 by 6 instead of 10 by 5. This bigger table is what makes the next step's arrangement possible.

keyTerms.meaning: the showbread, twelve loaves placed on the שולחן every שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The bread is the same size in both opinions. Only the table changes, so do not mix up which number belongs to which object.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
The Table – its length is twelve [handbreadths],
and its width is six;
the showbread – its length is ten,
and its width is five.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הַשֻּׁלְחָן אׇרְכּוֹ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion, against רבי יהודה's 10 by 5 table from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שולחן is 12 by 6 טפחים; the לחם הפנים is 10 by 5.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's arrangement with a gap in the middle for air
steps.stepSummary: Each loaf's length lies across the table's width, two טפחים are folded up on each side, and a two-טפח gap is left in the middle for air.
steps.simpleTranslation: He lays the loaf's length across the table's width, folds up two handbreadths on this side and two on that side, and leaves two handbreadths of space in the middle so the wind can blow between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר explains how the loaves sit on his larger table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 10-טפח loaf on a 6-טפח-wide table sticks out 4 טפחים, so 2 are folded up on each side, the same idea רבי יהודה had in step 11. What is new is the length of the table: two stacks of 5-wide loaves take up 10 of the 12 טפחים, leaving a 2-טפח gap in the middle. The gap lets air flow so the bread stays fresh.

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אׇרְכּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד רׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוּלְחָן,
phrases.english: He places its length across the width of the Table,
he folds up two handbreadths on this side
and two handbreadths on that side,
and two handbreadths of space in the middle,
so that the wind will blow between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹתֵן אׇרְכּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד רׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל שׁוּלְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי מאיר's statement, applying his measurements to the arrangement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves lie across the table, are folded up two טפחים on each side, and a two-טפח air gap is left between the two stacks.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's bigger table creates a 2-טפח gap between the two stacks for air.

steps.title: אבא שאול says the לבונה bowls sat in the gap
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול says the two bowls of לבונה for the לחם הפנים were placed in the middle gap.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: There they would place the two bowls of frankincense of the showbread.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול adds a use for רבי מאיר's middle gap: that is where the לבונה bowls went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gave the gap one purpose, letting air through. אבא שאול says it also held the two bowls of לבונה, so the לבונה was next to the bread, not on top of it. This position sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: bowls (the small bowls that held the frankincense)

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
There they would place
the two bowls of frankincense
of the showbread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: שָׁם הָיוּ נוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי מאיר's gap and gives it a further use.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two bowls of לבונה were placed in the gap between the two stacks.

steps.title: The חכמים object from the פסוק saying the לבונה goes on the arrangement
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that the פסוק says the לבונה goes "on" the stack, not next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But it already says, "And you shall place pure frankincense on the arrangement"!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge אבא שאול with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עַל usually means "on top of." If the לבונה must go on the stack itself, it cannot sit in a gap beside the stacks. So the פסוק seems to go against אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: on, upon (or, as the answer will argue, next to)

phrases.english: They said to him:
But surely it has already been stated:
"And you shall place pure frankincense on the arrangement"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אבא שאול's placement of the לבונה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבא שאול's claim that the bowls sat in the gap beside the loaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says עַל, meaning on top of the stack, not beside it.

steps.title: אבא שאול answers that עַל can mean 'next to'
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול points to "וְעָלָיו מַטֵּה מְנַשֶּׁה," where עַל means next to, not on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: But it already says, "And next to him shall be the tribe of מנשה."
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול answers the challenge by showing that the word עַל can mean "next to."
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the camp of the שבטים, מנשה camped beside אפרים, not on top of him, yet the פסוק still uses עָלָיו. So עַל הַמַּעֲרֶכֶת can mean beside the stack, and the bowls in the gap fit the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: and next to him (here meaning beside, not on top)

steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול reads עַל as "next to," so the לבונה sat beside the loaves in the middle gap.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Surely it has already been stated:
"And next to him shall be the tribe of Manasseh."
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' challenge from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the key word of the challenging פסוק using a parallel פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עַל must mean on top, so the לבונה cannot be in the gap.
steps.terutzMaskana: עַל can mean next to, as with מנשה, so the bowls beside the loaves fit the פסוק.

steps.title: The four golden panels and twenty-eight hollow rods
steps.stepSummary: Four golden panels, split at the top, held up the loaves, two per stack, along with 28 half-reed-shaped rods, 14 per stack.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were four golden panels there, split at their tops, which supported the bread, two for this stack and two for that stack. There were twenty-eight rods shaped like half of a hollow reed, fourteen for this stack and fourteen for that stack.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing the שולחן, listing the golden supports and rods that held the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The panels were split at the top so the rods could rest on them. The 28 rods were shaped like half a hollow reed, and they kept the loaves apart and supported them. Everything is split evenly between the two stacks.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַרְבָּעָה סְנִיפִין שֶׁל זָהָב הָיוּ שָׁם,
phrases.english: And there were four panels of gold there,
split at their tops,
with which they would support [the bread],
two for this arrangement
phrases.notes: "Arrangement" here means one of the two stacks of loaves.

phrases.english: and two for that arrangement,
and twenty-eight rods
like half of a hollow reed,
fourteen for this arrangement
and fourteen for that arrangement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַרְבָּעָה סְנִיפִין שֶׁל זָהָב הָיוּ שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the size and arrangement of the loaves to the physical supports on the שולחן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four forked golden panels (two per stack) and 28 half-reed rods (fourteen per stack) supported the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: The rods do not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: Arranging or removing the קנים does not push aside שבת. The כהן removes them on ערב שבת and lays them along the length of the שולחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Neither putting the rods in place nor taking them out pushes aside שבת. Instead, the כהן goes in on Friday, slides each rod out, and lays it along the length of the table.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that handling the קנים is not important enough to push aside שבת. It tells us what the כהן does instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the לחם הפנים on שבת itself is required, so it does push aside שבת. The rods are only a support, so working with them does not. The כהן removes them before שבת so that on שבת he only has to set down the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The half-reed-shaped rods placed between the loaves (from step 17)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up: the bread itself is changed on שבת. Only the work with the rods is moved to Friday.

phrases.english: Neither the arranging of the rods
nor their removal overrides שבת;
rather, he enters on Friday, before שבת,
and slides each one out, and places it along the length of the table.
phrases.notes: He pulls each rod out from between the loaves and lays it down on the table.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא סִידּוּר קָנִים וְלֹא נְטִילָתָם דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the שבת rule for the rods described in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handling the קנים does not override שבת. They are removed on ערב שבת and laid along the length of the שולחן.

steps.title: All Temple vessels lie along the length of the building
steps.stepSummary: Every כלי in the מקדש was placed with its long side running along the long side of the בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the vessels in the מקדש were placed so that their length ran along the length of the בית.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a general rule about how every כלי in the מקדש was positioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This includes the שולחן. Its long side ran in the same direction as the long side of the building, east to west.

keyTerms.meaning: The vessels / furnishings of the מקדש
The length of the בית (the Sanctuary building)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here. The שולחן, like every כלי, lies lengthwise along the בית, and the קנים are handled before שבת.

phrases.english: All the vessels that were in the מקדש,
their length was along the length of the בית.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ אׇרְכָּן לְאׇרְכּוֹ שֶׁל בֵּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a general rule about how the vessels were positioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every כלי in the מקדש was placed lengthwise along the length of the בית.

steps.title: Where do we learn that every meal offering needs a vessel inside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that every מנחה involves a vessel action inside. רבי is asked for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: All the meal offerings have a vessel action done inside. They asked רבי: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes the first rule of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up רבי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated a rule without a source. The question is where the requirement for a כלי שרת, done inside the עזרה, comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A step done with a sacred vessel (כלי שרת)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: All the meal offerings
have a vessel action done inside.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the line from the משנה about the מנחות needing a vessel inside.

phrases.english: They asked רבי: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the end of the משנה and returns to its opening rule to look for a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that every מנחה needs a כלי, used inside the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי quotes the פסוק in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי quotes a פסוק in יחזקאל. It names one inner place where the חטאת and אשם are cooked and the מנחה is baked, so they are not brought out to the outer courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Look, the פסוק says: "And he said to me: This is the place where the כהנים shall cook the חטאת and the אשם, where they shall bake the מנחה, so they are not brought out to the outer courtyard."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers with a פסוק. It puts the מנחה in the same inner place as the חטאת and the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the מנחה with the חטאת and אשם and keeps all three inside. The next step explains how this link proves the need for a כלי.

phrases.english: He said to them: Look, it says
"And he said to me: This is the place
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 46:20

phrases.english: where the priests shall cook
the sin offering and the guilt offering,
where they shall bake the meal offering,
so as not to bring them out to the outer courtyard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in יחזקאל 46:20 groups the מנחה with the חטאת and אשם, all prepared inside.

steps.title: The meal offering is like the sin and guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק groups the מנחה with the אשם and חטאת, it shares their rule. They need a כלי, so the מנחה needs a כלי too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מנחה is like the אשם and חטאת. Just as the אשם and חטאת need a vessel, the מנחה also needs a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי spells out how the פסוק proves the rule. Because the מנחה is listed together with the אשם and חטאת, it follows their rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking the meat of the אשם and חטאת is done in a vessel, inside the עזרה. Being listed with them shows that the מנחה is also prepared in a כלי, inside. This answers the question of step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as… so too… (the form of a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: The source for "every מנחה needs a כלי inside" is יחזקאל 46:20. There the מנחה is listed with the חטאת and אשם, which need a vessel.

phrases.english: The meal offering is like the guilt offering and the sin offering:
just as the guilt offering and the sin offering require a vessel,
so too the meal offering also requires a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 21 proves the rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מנחה, listed with the אשם and חטאת, shares their need for a כלי, used inside.

steps.title: How high the Table's holiness reaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'the שולחן is ten long.' Then רבי יוחנן figures the holy height above the שולחן. It is fifteen טפחים if two and a half are folded up, and twelve טפחים if two are folded up.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Table is ten long. רבי יוחנן said: according to the one who says two and a half handbreadths are folded up, the Table makes things holy fifteen handbreadths up. According to the one who says two handbreadths are folded up, it makes things holy twelve handbreadths up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה about the size of the שולחן. רבי יוחנן then works out a result from the two views in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pile has six loaves stacked one on another, and each loaf's folded-up sides stand at a certain height. רבי יהודה says two and a half טפחים are folded, so six loaves reach fifteen. רבי מאיר says two טפחים are folded, so six loaves reach twelve. The שולחן's holiness covers the whole height of the stack.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden Table in the היכל that holds the לחם הפנים
Folds up, meaning the sides of the loaf are bent upward
Makes holy, giving the קדושה of the vessel to what is placed on it
A handbreadth, a unit of measure

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the שולחן's holiness is not limited to its surface. It reaches up through the whole stack of bread.

phrases.english: The Table, its length is ten.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. It means ten handbreadths, and it opens a new topic.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
According to the one who says he folds up two and a half handbreadths,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.

phrases.english: it turns out the Table makes holy
fifteen handbreadths upward.
According to the one who says he folds up two handbreadths,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: it turns out the Table makes holy
twelve handbreadths upward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the source for a כלי and moves to the משנה's measurements of the שולחן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שולחן's holiness reaches fifteen טפחים up according to רבי יהודה and twelve according to רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Don't the rods add height?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's numbers. The קנים lie between the loaves, so the stack should be taller.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the rods!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of fifteen or twelve. It points out that there are קנים between the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן counted only the height of the loaves. If קנים sit between each loaf, they should add to the total height, and then his numbers would be too low.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is, a word that opens a challenge
Rods placed between the loaves of לחם הפנים

phrases.english: But aren't there rods?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the height calculation of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's totals of fifteen and twelve טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קנים between the loaves should add height beyond the loaves alone.

steps.title: The rods sink into the loaves
steps.stepSummary: The קנים are sunk into the loaves, so they add no height.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rods are sunk into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The קנים sit down inside the loaves, so they do not add anything to the height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves were shaped so the קנים settle into them. Because of this, the stack is only as tall as the loaves themselves, and רבי יוחנן's numbers stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinks them in, so they are fully set into the loaves

phrases.english: The rods, he sinks them in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קנים sit on top of the loaves and add height.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנים are sunk into the loaves and add no height.

steps.title: Why are the rods there?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the purpose of the קנים is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the קנים are needed at all. This question sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before it can test the answer that the קנים are sunk in, the גמרא first needs to know what the קנים are for.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the rods are needed in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Prepares a challenge to the answer of step 25.

steps.title: To keep the bread from going moldy
steps.stepSummary: The קנים are there so the bread does not get moldy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the bread getting moldy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The קנים keep the bread from getting moldy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנים let air pass between the loaves. Without them, the loaves would press together and grow mold during the week they sit on the שולחן.

phrases.english: Because of the bread getting moldy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קנים let air reach the loaves so the bread does not grow mold.

steps.title: Sunk-in rods won't stop mold
steps.stepSummary: If the קנים are sunk into the loaves, the loaves touch, and the bread will still get moldy.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, the bread gets moldy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 25. If the קנים are fully sunk in, they cannot do their job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנים are supposed to make a gap for air. If they sink all the way into the loaves, there is no gap, and the mold problem comes back.

phrases.english: In the end, the bread gets moldy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the purpose from step 27 to challenge the answer of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the קנים are sunk into the loaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fully sunk קנים leave no air gap, so they cannot prevent mold.

steps.title: The rods are lifted a little
steps.stepSummary: The כהן raises the קנים a little, which leaves a small gap for air.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raises it a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the קנים are lifted slightly. They are not pushed in all the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנים are mostly sunk in, so they barely add height, but they stick up a little. That small gap lets air reach the bread. This keeps both points: the height count stays basically the same, and the bread stays fresh.
steps.whatToRemember: The שולחן makes things holy up to the top of the bread stack: fifteen טפחים according to רבי יהודה and twelve according to רבי מאיר. The קנים are sunk into the loaves, so they add no real height. They are raised a little so air can stop the bread from getting moldy.

phrases.english: That he raises it a little.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rods. They sit mostly inside the loaves but stick up just enough for air to get through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קנים are fully sunk in, which leaves no air gap.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנים are slightly raised, leaving a small gap for air without adding real height.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קנים are mostly sunk in but raised slightly, so they prevent mold without changing the height count.

steps.title: The small gaps should add height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the כהן raises the קנים to leave a gap for air, those small gaps should add to the height of each stack.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is that little bit of space between the loaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If there is a small air gap between each loaf, the stack should end up taller than the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said the כהן lifts the קנים a little so air can flow. But six loaves with five gaps means extra height, so the total should be more than the number we counted.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is (a challenge pointing to something left out)
A little bit, a small amount

phrases.english: But isn't there that little bit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 29 by pointing out a side effect of raising the קנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The height count of the bread stacks, after step 29's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Raising the קנים creates gaps, and gaps add height that the count did not include.

steps.title: Gaps smaller than a טפח are not counted
steps.stepSummary: Since all the gaps together do not reach a טפח, they are not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it does not add up to a טפח, he does not count it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the gaps are too small to matter. Since they do not reach a full טפח, they are left out of the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The height is counted in whole טפחים. A tiny extra amount that is less than one טפח is not big enough to change the number.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a unit of measure

phrases.english: Since it is not a full handbreadth,
he does not count it.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, who counted fifteen or twelve handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי טֶפַח, לָא חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Too small to count: the amount is below the unit of measure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every bit of extra height, even the small gaps, should be added to the total.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gaps adding up to less than a טפח are left out of the count.

steps.title: The frankincense bowls should add height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the בזיכין of frankincense are also on the שולחן, so they should add to the height.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the bowls of frankincense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second thing that seems to be left out: the בזיכין that go with the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bowls sat on top of the stacks, they would make the whole arrangement taller. So the height count would seem too low.

keyTerms.meaning: The bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים
Frankincense, the spice inside the bowls

phrases.english: But there are the bowls!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the gaps are answered, a second item that might add height is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: The height count of the arrangement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בזיכין take up space too, so their height should be counted.

steps.title: The bowls sit inside the bread
steps.stepSummary: The בזיכין rested inside the bread, at the same level as the bread, so they add no height.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat inside the bread, and they stood level with the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bowls were set down into the bread, not on top of it, so they do not make anything taller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the bowls were placed among the loaves, their height was the same as the bread's. The total height stays the same.

phrases.english: they would sit inside the bread,
and they would stand level with the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the setup: the item does not stick out above the bread
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בזיכין sat on top of the stacks and added height.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בזיכין sat inside the bread, level with it, so they add nothing.

steps.title: The horn-like corners should add height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the loaves have קרנות, horn-like corners that stick up, so they should add height.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the horns!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third thing that seems to be left out: the קרנות on the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves have corners that rise up like horns. If they stick up, each loaf is taller than its flat body, and the stack should be taller.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn-like corners that rise up from the loaves

phrases.english: But there are the horns!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bowls are answered, a third item that might add height is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: The height count of the arrangement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרנות stick up from the loaves, so they should add to the total height.

steps.title: The horns are folded in under the next loaf
steps.stepSummary: The כהן folds the קרנות into the bread, and the loaf above rests on them, so they add no height.
steps.simpleTranslation: He folds the horns into the bread, and the bread above rests on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the horns are bent inward, and the next loaf sits on top of them, so they do not raise the stack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרנות do not stick up freely. They are pressed into the loaf and covered by the loaf above, so the stack's height stays as counted.
steps.whatToRemember: Three things seemed to add height: the air gaps, the בזיכין, and the קרנות. None of them change the count. The gaps are less than a טפח, the bowls sit inside the bread, and the horns are folded under the loaf above.

phrases.english: the horns, he folds them into the bread,
and the bread rests on them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34 and ends this run of height challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the setup: the item is folded in and covered
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קרנות stick up and add to the height of the stack.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קרנות are folded into the bread under the loaf above, so they add no height.
